Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 27 (*Sakkaccapaṭiggahaṇa*, "Not receiving respectfully") is a training rule (*sekhiya*) belonging to the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga of the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule regulates monastic decorum regarding the proper manner of receiving almsfood with respect [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the text is provided on SuttaCentral by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Parallels to this rule are widely attested across early Buddhist traditions, including the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Vinaya recensions (Prātimokṣas and Vibhaṅgas) of the Dharmaguptaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Mahīśāsaka, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Sarvāstivāda, Kāśyapīya, and Lokottaravāda traditions preserved in Chinese, Tibetan, and Sanskrit, alongside internal Pali parallels in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and the Parivāra [SuttaCentral]. All candidate citations found in the reference literature refer either to verse 27 of the Sāṅkhyakārikā or to Tibetan hagiographical literature rather than this Vinaya rule.
